title.narrative: Multitranche Financing Facility (MFF) - Small and Medium Enterprise Investment Program Tranche 3

description.narrative: Tranche 3 will help Damu continue with the implementation of the government's Action Plan to increase access to medium term finance for SMEs. The funds will be relent in local currency (tenge) fixed-interest loans to qualified participating financial institutions (PFIs) to fund their respective market-based loans, leases and other financial products to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

SMEs have increased access to medium term credit on a sustainable basis.

By the end of 2016 Under Damu programs, SME lending increased to T1,042 billion (baseline: T750 billion in 2013) Progress/Status: On the disbursement side, three out of four participating financial institutions (PFIs) witness severe solvency issues since 2016. By the latest developments, KKB has fully prepaid its loan of US$82.30 million as of end April 2017. Likewise, KIB has fully prepaid its loan of US$9.7 million to Damu and ADB has received the prepayment last 24 July 2017. Last 21 April 2014 Damu announced a default on Delta Bank due to instability of its operations. Damu shall fully prepay the loan back to ADB this November 2017 due to non-feasibility of transferring the loan portfolio to other banks. Lastly, Tsesna Bank has partially prepaid an amount of US$14.20 million to Damu then to returned to ADB as portion of their unutilized loan allocation.
